body: The Holmenkollen Ski festival is held every March in Oslo and is one of Norway's most loved winter traditions. The festival was first celebrated in 1892, and it began as a gathering of people who traveled on skis to watch exciting ski jumps and cross-country races. Today, it remains a symbol of Norwegian culture and blends sport with tradition. At the heart of the festival is the iconic Holmenkollen Ski Jump, a towering structure that offers beautiful views of Oslo. Here, world-class athletes compete in front of thousands of cheering fans. Beyond the competitions, the festival brings people together in a warm and lively atmosphere. Families and friends gather outdoors to enjoy the winter. Visitors can explore the world's oldest ski museum, climb the jump tower for amazing views, or try fun activities like ziplining. Also, the festival streets are filled with food trucks and music. And of course, you can taste traditional Norwegian waffles. Holmenkollen is more than a sporting event. It is a celebration of nature, tradition, and national pride. For those who love winter, skiing, and cultural experiences, this historic festival is a must-see.
